current.title: Child Mortality Fell 60% Since 1990
current.hook: Child deaths used to be brutal. Not anymore.
current.closing: Progress doesn't announce itself. It just quietly happens.
current.question: Did you get your shots as a kid? Tell me below.

segments.say: In 1990, the under-5 mortality rate was 93.5 per thousand live births. By 2024 it fell to 37.4 — a 60 percent drop in one generation.

segments.topic: the fix behind falling child mortality: immunization
segments.say: The fix wasn't fancy. DPT immunization coverage climbed from 17 percent in 1980 to 85 percent of kids today — one shot, given almost everywhere.

segments.topic: health spending behind the falling child mortality
segments.say: And the world backed it with money — health spending rose from 8.6 percent of global GDP in 2000 to 10.1 percent by 2023, funding the shot.

judge.one_line: A chart slideshow: gauge, line, columns, bars. It opens on 8 seconds of a static-looking gauge and ends on a clipped health-spending stack instead of the 60% drop.
problems: The hook (hook@0.3 to seg0:end) is a slow gauge with a title card that holds one layout for about 8s. It gives no reason to stay.
seg1, seg2 and seg3 are stock charts (line, columns, bars). None of them makes a child death or a vaccine visible.
In seg0 the mascot stands pointing inside a box for about 8s, and in seg3 he walks along the bars with no purpose.
The closing (seg4) is about health spending, not mortality, so the payoff never lands the 60% drop.
In seg4:mid through payoff@-0.4 the year and value labels have their tops sliced off.
In seg3:start the bars are near-empty with no values showing, and a 1.5-point rise from 8.6 to 10.1 on a stretched bar reads as no change.
fixes: Open on motion that shows the stat. For example, 94 child figures with about 56 of them turning safe in the first 2 seconds.
Replace the seg0 gauge with a demonstration made of children, and give Data a setup, action and payoff. For example, he shields figures as the rate falls.
Show immunization as syringes or kids receiving a shot, filling from 17 of 100 to 85 of 100, instead of columns.
Tie spending to the outcome visually, or cut it. Do not end on it.
End on the 93.5 to 37.4 reveal. Measure and clamp every label inside the safe area, and drop the 'what he's carrying' caption.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.
